passage: I sit two rows behind Sumit, so I saw most of it. For weeks Manoj had been taking Sumit's pencil case and laughing when Sumit reached for it. At recess on Thursday Manoj did it again, and Sumit shoved him hard against the railing with both hands. Manoj fell and yelled, and then the teacher on duty was there. Sumit's face was red and his eyes looked wet, though I can't say if that was anger or fear. Both boys were marched to the principal's office. Sumit came back with a note in his diary for home. I'm Nisha, by the way, and I wish I had said something sooner.

qa.q: What did Sumit do to Manoj at recess on Thursday?
qa.a: Sumit shoved Manoj hard against the railing with both hands.

qa.q: What might Sumit have been feeling when the teacher on duty arrived?
qa.a: Probably angry and frightened at once, since his face was red and his eyes looked wet, though Nisha admits it is hard to be sure.

qa.q: What approach could Sumit have used instead of pushing, and why?
qa.a: He could have told the teacher about the pencil case being taken, because the taking would be dealt with and Sumit would not end up in trouble too.

qa.q: How might Manoj have seen the push?
qa.a: Manoj may have been shocked and hurt, and for that day it turned the bully into the one who was pushed, which is the opposite of what Sumit wanted.

grounding: A boy pushes the bully at recess and both are sent to the principal, so revenge leaves him in trouble too.
